VERDICT: ACCEPT

The arithmetic checks out. With $A=(s-1)(1+\gamma)-2s = s\gamma-s-\gamma-1$ and $B=s(\gamma-1)=s\gamma-s$, we get $A+B=2s\gamma-2s-\gamma-1$, which equals the proposed $2s\gamma-\gamma-2s-1$.

The endpoints follow from the power-solution scaling. Matching exponents gives $\beta=(\alpha+2s)/(1+\gamma)$, and a positive solution $c\,x_n^\beta$ requires $\lambda(s,\beta)>0$, i.e. $\beta\in(s-1,s)$. Inverting this gives the stated interval for $\alpha$. As a check, at $s=1$ it reduces to $(-2,\gamma-1)$, the classical local range.

The "if and only if" part is not verified here. The answer depends on the claim that no non-power solutions exist outside this range, and I could not confirm that against the source result. Its sharpness is the main uncertainty.

CONFIDENCE: 3
